assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Which commands are synchronous and leave a trace

muse's registered slash-command roster (dumped from the shipped binary `~/.local/bin/muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1` via `strings`) includes `/usage` (aliased `/cost`, `/context` — "Show session usage") and `/status` ("Show current session status"), both plainly local-display commands with no model-invocation semantics in their descriptions — mirroring the claudecode/antigravity sibling cells' `/cost` and `/help` picks. Both are LIVE-CONFIRMED synchronous and DO leave a durable trace, just not the one that reaches the daemon's events.jsonl (see below):

- `/usage`: session `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/13/01a09c49-8dbd-7150-b70d-15f527a633d3/session.jsonl` (25 lines) contains NINE consecutive `command.invoked{command:"/usage"}` records (lines 16-24) as the session's last activity — no other `payload_type` follows the first invocation. Confirms `/usage` is purely local: no model call, no other side-effecting record.
- `/status`: session `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/01a09ed0-752c-75e1-b223-c5bd24e17876/session.jsonl` (18 lines, recorded live today) invokes `/upgrade` then `/status` back to back (lines 15 and 17) with a `session.subscription_entrypoint.impression` between them (a durable side-effect specific to `/upgrade`, not `/status`) — `/status`'s own invocation is the LAST line of the file: nothing follows it. Confirms `/status` too is purely local with no model call.

`/model` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this recipe: it opens an arrow-key picker and silently ignores an inline argument (live-confirmed by the 5.2 model-identification assessment, cited in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`'s MODEL-pin comment), and the interactive driver's `keys` step type is `not_implemented` (`driver-interactive.sh` line ~671: `keys) not_implemented keys …`). Picking `/usage`+`/status` sidesteps that gap entirely rather than freezing on it.

## The daemon pillar: full, on a NEGATIVE claim

The scenario's four acceptance bullets (state stays ready throughout; no -> working transition for the slash command; final state ready; tool calls <= 0) are all claims about the ABSENCE of a transition, not about surfacing the slash command's own content. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`'s `route()` switch (lines 227-232) handles `payloadTypeCommandInvoked` by setting `ev.Skip = true` with the comment "A slash command (/model, /usage, /exit -- format-spec S10) ... Bookkeeping, not a turn boundary." `parser_test.go`'s `TestParseLine_CommandInvoked_Skipped` (lines 465-471) pins this as a regression test. Per the adapter contract, turn boundaries ONLY fire on `("run","started")`/`("run","terminal")` events; `command.invoked` is neither, so no `state_transition` is ever derived from it -- the session simply stays in whatever state it was already in (ready).

This is exactly the shape claudecode's sibling cell established for `/cost`+`/help` (its parser's `isLocalCommandContent` filter) and antigravity's sibling cell established for `/help` (recorded in a sibling `history.jsonl` the Source never tails) -- muse's own version of the same architectural fact, evidenced by ITS OWN parser code and ITS OWN live corpus rather than assumed from the template.

## Observation-vs-emission caveat (the vacuous-pass condition)

`command.invoked` is Skip=true, so it NEVER reaches `events.jsonl` -- the daemon's own event stream carries no positive trace that a slash command was invoked at all. The scenario's phase assertions (session stays `ready`, no `working` transition) would ALSO pass if the recipe's `slash` driver step silently failed to send anything to the muse REPL -- "nothing happened" and "a no-op slash command happened" are indistinguishable from events.jsonl alone. This is the Vacuous-pass rule's textbook case. Mitigation: `record`'s verify step MUST additionally grep the recording's raw transcript (muse's `session.jsonl`, archived as this cell's `transcript.jsonl`) for two `command.invoked` records naming `/usage` and `/status` -- confirming the driver's `slash` steps actually reached the REPL -- since expected.jsonl's phase DSL has no vocabulary to assert content inside a Skip=true record. This is named explicitly as a caveat and as a recipe precondition below, not left implicit.

## Why no warm-up turn is needed (unlike claudecode/antigravity)

claudecode and antigravity's sibling cells both open with a real "warm" turn before the slash window, because their transcript file only materializes after the first genuine LLM turn. muse does not share that constraint: `route_facts`/`metadata`/the permission-profile `retained_frame` are all written to `session.jsonl` at session OPEN, before any prompt (muse-format-spec.md S2; independently confirmed live in both cited sessions above, neither of which contains a single `run`/turn event yet both have a fully-formed `session.jsonl` from `session.opened.observed` onward). The already-recorded sibling cell `1-1_session-start` and `2-1_basic-turn` (both `observed`/recorded in this same replaydata tree) assert `session_birth: ready, relative_to: start` with NO warm-up phase, and both pass live -- so this recipe issues the two slash commands directly after session birth, matching the scenario's own process description ("1. Agent is in ready. 2. User invokes a no-LLM slash command...") instead of claudecode/antigravity's transcript-materialization workaround.

## Driver pillar

`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`'s `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean restart sigkill start_session session"` (line 167) lists `slash` and `send` as genuinely ported step types (not stubbed) -- `case ... send|slash) step_send ...` (line 667) treats a slash command exactly like ordinary text+Enter, which is all `/usage` and `/status` need (no picker, no follow-up keystrokes). No driver gap.
caveats: command.invoked never reaches events.jsonl (Skip=true, per parser.go) -- the phase system can only assert the ABSENCE of a state transition, not the PRESENCE of the slash invocation itself. A silently-failed driver `slash` step would pass the same phases. record's verify step must additionally grep the recording's raw transcript.jsonl for two command.invoked records (/usage, /status) as a positive check the phase DSL cannot express -- named as a recipe precondition below.

/model is excluded on purpose: it opens an arrow-key picker (silently ignores an inline argument) and the interactive driver's `keys` step is not_implemented -- using it here would manufacture a driver-gap route for a scenario that doesn't need one.

/exit is excluded on purpose: format-spec S10 confirms it's real and synchronous, but it tears the session down -- incompatible with 'a tiny normal prompt to prove the session is still alive' afterward.

Neither cited live session actually reached a real model turn (both are pure slash-command probes), so the 'daemon stays full while a REAL turn later returns ready->working->ready' half of this cell's claim rests on the already-recorded 2-1_basic-turn sibling cell's turn mechanics, not on these two sessions directly -- the two are cited only for the slash-command-is-inert half.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1 per replaydata/agents/muse/metadata.json)
muse auth complete: 'muse login' (Meta account, browser code approval) or META_API_KEY exported -- auth is set up out-of-band, the rig's precheck delegates it to the user
tmux available -- the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL
irrlichd is recording -- either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record

record's verify step must grep the recording's transcript.jsonl (muse's raw session.jsonl) for two command.invoked records naming /usage and /status -- the daemon's own events.jsonl carries no trace of either (Skip=true), so this is the only positive confirmation that the slash steps actually reached the REPL rather than silently no-opping
setup: The interactive driver creates a fresh empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/ and launches `muse --trust-workspace` in a tmux session there, then sleeps 1s for muse's own input handler to wire up before the first send
--trust-workspace is REQUIRED: every staging cwd is brand-new, so muse's 'Do you trust this workspace?' modal fires on every run and would eat the first slash command without it
Avoid /model (opens an arrow-key picker; keys step not_implemented) and /exit (tears the session down, incompatible with the trailing 'still alive' prompt) -- use /usage and /status only
muse mints its own session UUID on launch; the driver resolves the newest session.jsonl under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions (excluding subagent/ copies) newer than a pre-launch marker

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl mints the session in ready shortly after muse's TUI finishes launching (single-birth; session id from the session directory basename == stream.id)
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to working or waiting for at least 5s after session birth -- the /usage + /status window

the recording's raw transcript.jsonl (muse's session.jsonl) contains two command.invoked records, command=/usage and command=/status, confirming the slash steps actually reached the REPL (this is the positive check events.jsonl cannot provide -- see the assessment's caveats)

events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working when the final 'Reply with exactly the word: ok' prompt lands, then back to ready when it completes -- proving the session is still alive after the slash window
no function_call/tool-call event occurs anywhere in the recording (tool_calls_max: 0 per the scenario's acceptance criteria)
final session state is ready before exit_clean tears the REPL down
observation vector: tokens_nonzero=true (the final real turn), cost_nonzero=false (model unpriced in the litellm catalog), model unpinned
